clips.text: We did it! You built the whole bridge.
Pip needs a bridge to roll across the sky. Bridges need gems!
Island A… or island B?
One, two. Two gems.
One, two, three, four. Four gems.
Look at both islands. Take your time.
Let’s match them up. One gem from each island, then look for leftovers.
See the leftovers? The island with leftovers has more.
Match, match. Two left over!
Which island has more gems?
Yes! Four is more than two. Bridge, go!
Island A… or island B?
One, two, three, four, five. Five gems.
One, two, three, four. Four gems.
Close ones are tricky. Count each island slowly.
Let’s match them up and look for a leftover.
Five and four. Five is more, so this island has more.
Match, match, match, match. One left over!
Ooh, these are close. Which island has more gems?
Yes! Five is more than four. Just one more!
Island A… or island B?
One, two, three. Three gems.
One, two, three, four, five. Five gems.
Spread-out gems can look like a lot. Check carefully.
Let’s match them up and see who has leftovers.
Three and five. The bunched-up island has more!
Match, match, match. Two left over!
Tricky one! Some gems are spread out. Which island has more?
You checked! Five is more than three, even bunched up.
Island A… or island B?
One, two, three, four, five, six. Six gems.
One, two, three, four. Four gems.
Big gems take up more room. That doesn’t mean more gems.
Match them up. Who has leftovers?
Six little gems and four big gems. Six is more!
Match, match, match, match. Two left over!
One more tricky one. Big gems or little gems. Which island has more?
Yes! Six is more than four, even when they’re small.
Island A, island B, or the same?
One, two, three, four. Four gems.
One, two, three, four. Four gems.
Look closely. Could they be the same?
Match them up. Are there any leftovers?
No leftovers! Four and four. They’re the same.
Match, match, match, match. No leftovers. They’re the same!
Which island has more? Or are they the same?
The same! Four and four. That’s called equal.
Island A… or island B?
One, two, three. Three gems.
One, two, three, four, five, six. Six gems.
Look at both islands again.
Match them up and look for leftovers.
Three and six. Six is more!
Match, match, match. Three left over!
Bonus! Which island has more gems?
Yes! Six is more than three.
Two, three, or four?
One, two, three. Three gems.
One, two, three, four, five, six. Six gems.
Match them up, then count only the leftovers.
Let’s match them up. Now count the leftovers.
Three left over. Six is three more than three.
Match, match, match. Three left over!
How many more gems are on the island with six?
Yes! Three more. Six is three more than three.
Five gems! Pip’s bridge is getting longer.
Pip’s collection is growing. Let’s find five gems.
Group A, group B, or group C?
Touch each gem once as you count.
Point and say one number for each gem. Stop after five.
Look at the glowing group. One, two, three, four, five!
Which group has five gems?
One, two, three, four, five. Five gems altogether!
Three gems for Pip’s bridge. Nice counting!
Pip is collecting gems for a bridge. Let’s find a little group.
Group A, group B, or group C?
Point at each gem as you count.
Count slowly: one, two, three. Then stop.
Look at the glowing group. One, two, three!
Which group has three gems?
One, two, three. This group has three gems!
Click! The shape lock opens.
Pip’s gate has a shape lock. Shapes have clues. Follow their edges with your finger.
Square, circle, or triangle?
Square, triangle, or circle?
Circle, square, or triangle?
Circle, triangle, or square?
Triangle, square, or circle?
Triangle, circle, or square?
Trace each shape’s edges with your finger.
Count the straight sides. A triangle has three sides and three corners.
Look at the glowing shape. One, two, three sides!
Which shape has three straight sides?
A triangle has three straight sides and three corners.
The lights keep blinking. Great pattern spotting!
The bridge lights blink in a pattern. Listen to their rhythm.
Triangle, circle, or square?
Triangle, square, or circle?
Circle, triangle, or square?
Circle, square, or triangle?
Square, triangle, or circle?
Square, circle, or triangle?
Say the pattern out loud with me.
Circle, triangle is the part that repeats. Start that pair again.
Circle, triangle, circle, triangle… circle!
Circle, triangle, circle, triangle. What comes next?
Circle comes next. Circle, triangle is the part that repeats.
Bonus round! Want to try a tricky one?
A Pip gate! Solve it to open the way.
Hi, I’m Pip! I roll across the sky islands.
Use the arrows, then press enter!
Press the letter!
Type the number!
Tap your answer!
Tilt to choose, then jump!
This bridge opens when Pip has one gem!
This bridge opens when Pip has ten gems!
This bridge opens when Pip has two gems!
This bridge opens when Pip has three gems!
This bridge opens when Pip has four gems!
This bridge opens when Pip has five gems!
This bridge opens when Pip has six gems!
This bridge opens when Pip has seven gems!
This bridge opens when Pip has eight gems!
This bridge opens when Pip has nine gems!
This bridge is locked. Solve Pip gate one first!
This bridge is locked. Solve Pip gate two first!
This bridge is locked. Solve Pip gate three first!
This bridge is locked. Solve Pip gate four first!
This bridge is locked. Solve Pip gate five first!
This bridge is locked. Solve Pip gate six first!
This bridge is locked. Solve Pip gate seven first!
This bridge is locked. Solve Pip gate eight first!
The finish is locked. Pip still needs your help!
This lift is locked. Help Pip first!
This bridge opens when you find the island!
Bring Pip one gem!
Bring Pip ten gems!
Bring Pip two gems!
Bring Pip three gems!
Bring Pip four gems!
Bring Pip five gems!
Bring Pip six gems!
Bring Pip seven gems!
Bring Pip eight gems!
Bring Pip nine gems!
That’s all the gems Pip needs. Thank you!
A Pip mission! Listen closely.
You found it!
Roll to the island with the fewest gems!
Roll to island A!
Roll to island B!
Roll to island C!
Roll to island D!
Roll to island E!
Roll to island F!
Roll to island G!
Roll to island H!
Roll to island I!
Roll to island J!
Roll to the island with the most gems!
Try the arrow keys!
Try pressing the letter!
Try typing the number!
Try tapping your answer!
Try tilting to choose!
One!
Ten!
Two!
Three!
Four!
Five!
Six!
Seven!
Eight!
Nine!
Oops! Pip’s gate first.
Oops! Solve Pip gate one first.
Oops! Solve Pip gate two first.
Oops! Solve Pip gate three first.
Oops! Solve Pip gate four first.
Oops! Solve Pip gate five first.
Oops! Solve Pip gate six first.
Oops! Solve Pip gate seven first.
Oops! Solve Pip gate eight first.
The gate is open. Let’s roll on!
The bridge is open!
The finish is open!
The lift is working!
The square family is together again!
Pip found a family of shapes. They belong together, even when their colors change.
Green circle, green square, or green triangle?
Green circle, green triangle, or green square?
Green square, green circle, or green triangle?
Green square, green triangle, or green circle?
Green triangle, green circle, or green square?
Green triangle, green square, or green circle?
Look at the shape, not the color.
Each square has four equal sides. Find another one.
Look at the glowing shape. It has four equal sides, like the others!
Which shape belongs with these squares?
The green square belongs. All of these shapes are squares.
